findings.title: R15 CreatePayment dispatch has no durable cross-restart one-shot guard or committed payment manifest
findings.counterexample: providerInvoked/workerInvoked are plain in-memory booleans (`let providerInvoked=false,workerInvoked=false;`). A serverless instance crash or redeploy between CreatePayment dispatch and receipt of/durable recording of the provider response resets these flags. A subsequent runOnce() call (manual retry, redeploy, or a second protected-Preview invocation) would issue a second live Square Sandbox CreatePayment for the same booking, because no docs/execution/p6/r15-evidence/payment-operation-manifest.json exists for R15 and no R15-specific exclusive/fsynced guard (the only such guard in the tree, tools/acceptance/s2-operator-guard.mjs, is bound to the old R9 S2 manifest hash and is explicitly documented as historical, not deployed R15 proof).
findings.impact: Real duplicate 100 JPY Sandbox charge and violation of Authority §22 (CreatePayment max 1, retry 0, UNKNOWN=DO_NOT_RETRY).
findings.test_coverage: tests/unit/r15-composition.test.ts only proves the in-memory latch rejects a second call within the SAME object instance (`assert.rejects(app.runOnce(),/R15_WORKER_ALREADY_INVOKED_DO_NOT_RETRY/)`); no test simulates process restart/new instance, so the cross-restart gap is structurally untestable with current code.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Add an exclusive, fsynced, filesystem-or-DB-backed guard (analogous to dispatchS2Once) keyed to a newly committed R15 payment-operation-manifest.json, and require it to be acquired before r15HostedComposition.runOnce() invokes the provider; the in-memory flags may remain as a secondary same-process check only.
findings.required_proof: A test that reconstructs the composition object (simulating restart) after a completed dispatch and shows the external guard — not the in-memory flag — blocks the second attempt, plus evidence the guard file survives an injected crash before fsync completes.

findings.title: Non-disclosing Square webhook signature-key handoff is documented intent only, not implemented
findings.counterexample: Authority §16 requires the Sandbox subscription-create response's signature key be consumed in-process into dedicated Vercel secret storage 'without showing/persisting it.' No script or module implementing this handoff exists anywhere in the supplied source tree; docs/execution/R15_DEVELOPMENT_ACTIVATION.md step 7 and CURRENT_SAFE_OPERATION_NOTE.missingLiveImplementation both list it as 'not implemented.' If Codex parent proceeds ad hoc when the time comes, there is no reviewed guarantee the value cannot transit a shell variable, stdout capture, or an evidence JSON file.
findings.impact: Potential exposure of a live Square webhook signature key, a Security Absolute explicitly forbidden by Authority §33 and Governance §5 (never Square tokens/keys to chat/log/repo).
findings.test_coverage: No test exists or can exist for an unimplemented mechanism; existing tests (square-webhook-receiver.test.ts, r15-ingress.test.ts) only validate parsing of an already-populated env var, not the acquisition/handoff path.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Implement and statically review a bounded in-process handoff function whose only side effect is writing to the target secret store, whose return value/thrown errors never include the key, before Authority §16 is executed.
findings.required_proof: Source of the handoff function plus a redacted-output test proving no return path, log call, or exception message can contain the raw key.

findings.title: Hosted Neon least-privilege design is unverified on the actual hosted resource; only local superuser-owned proof exists
findings.counterexample: All 21+ role/negative-privilege real-DB checks (tests/readiness/r14-postgres.ts, r14-additional.ts, r14-boundaries.ts) connect only to an embedded, test-runner-owned PostgreSQL cluster created via EmbeddedPostgres in scripts/postgres.ts (127.0.0.1, superuser-created roles). The created Neon resource store_i5vh0ZEKo2ikcVo9 has 0 connected projects, 0 migrations applied, 0 roles provisioned (per docs/execution/p6/r15-neon-resume/PROVISION_RESULT.md and the current-status JSON's hostedDbMigrations/hostedRoleTests: NOT_STARTED). Neon's own connection-pooling/proxy layer, default database grants, and role-management constraints have never been exercised.
findings.impact: Questions E and G ('does hosted execution actually match role design?' / 'local superuser proof is not hosted proof') cannot be answered PASS; an undetected Neon-specific difference (e.g., pooled SET LOCAL behavior, default PUBLIC grants on a freshly created database, or role creation limits under a managed Postgres) could silently weaken guarantees that were validated only locally.
findings.test_coverage: None of the reported 495-510 passing tests touch the hosted resource; JSON evidence labeled 'REAL_POSTGRESQL' refers exclusively to the local embedded cluster and could be misread as hosted proof if not read carefully.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Apply migrations 0001-0029 to the actual Neon namespace via migrateHostedDevelopment, provision the 6 roles via provisionHostedPaymentRoles, and rerun the equivalent role-negative-test suite directly against the hosted connection string before any ingress/webhook wiring references it.
findings.required_proof: Sanitized real-DB evidence JSON (matching the shape of db-final-metadata.json / real-db-tests.json) captured with the connection host verified as the Neon ep-*.neon.tech endpoint, not 127.0.0.1.

findings.title: Dedicated ingress install pulls the entire monorepo dependency graph, contrary to the stated minimization goal
findings.counterexample: installCommand runs `npm ci --prefix ../.. --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, installing every root dependency (better-auth, sharp, @aws-sdk/*, playwright, drizzle-orm, etc.) into the minimal-surface ingress deployment, though the bundled runtime.cjs (per scripts/build-ingress.mjs's metafile) only ever references the receiver/pg code path.
findings.impact: Larger on-disk dependency surface for an internet-facing 'receiver-only' project than Authority §3's '極小化' (minimize) goal intends; --ignore-scripts mitigates the primary postinstall-script supply-chain vector, so no direct exploit path is demonstrated — impact is unused code presence, not a proven route to code execution beyond the fixed 404/health/webhook routes already tested.
findings.test_coverage: tests/unit/r15-ingress.test.ts checks route surface, installCommand package-manager pin, and --ignore-scripts presence, but does not assert dependency-set minimization.
findings.minimum_safe_correction: Scope the install to only the packages actually referenced by the bundled artifact (already enumerated by esbuild's metafile.inputs), or explicitly accept this as a documented residual risk given --ignore-scripts.
findings.required_proof: None required to unblock activation; recommended hardening before treating the ingress project as long-lived infrastructure beyond the current acceptance window.
